nodes.name: Watch inbox
nodes.notes:
Needs an IMAP credential: host imap.gmail.com, port 993, SSL/TLS on, and the SAME Gmail app password as the SMTP credential. If Avast (or similar) is intercepting TLS, tick 'Allow Self-Signed Certificates' here — the NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS mount covers Node's own TLS, but this node has its own toggle.

postProcessAction is 'nothing': messages are left UNREAD and untouched. This workflow reads your mail, it does not manage it — marking things read behind your back would be a surprising side effect, and the backend already de-duplicates on message id.

IMAP requires enabling in Gmail: Settings -> Forwarding and POP/IMAP -> Enable IMAP.

nodes.name: Match and classify
nodes.notes:
The backend matches each message to an application and classifies it.

Only acknowledgements are applied automatically. Rejections, interview invitations and offers are recorded as SUGGESTIONS for you to confirm in the app, because acting on a misread would either abandon a live opportunity or claim progress that never happened.

Ambiguous mail — several open roles at one employer, nothing to tell them apart — is filed for review with no suggestion rather than attributed by guess.

Rescans are safe: the backend de-duplicates on message id, so the same reply is never suggested twice.

nodes.name: Did the scan fail?
nodes.notes: Unmatched mail is NOT a failure — most of your inbox is unrelated to job hunting, and the backend keeps unmatched messages for review anyway. Only a non-2xx response counts.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ workflow: 'WF-F', message: ($json.error?.message || `inbox scan failed (HTTP ${$json.statusCode || '?'})`), context: { execution_id: $execution.id, detail: $json } }) }}
